title: Going Global: 39 Language Versions of the BFI-2-XS
venue: Measurement Instruments for the Social Sciences, 2025, Vol. 7, Article e14067
document_type: academic-article (instrument documentation and translation-procedure report, no respondent-level data)
coverage: Full text read end to end: 1492 lines of the 54,597-char text file, in four chunks (front matter, abstract, introduction, method, Table 1 and Table 2 layout text, results, discussion, supplementary-materials note, references). Figures 1 and 2 are image-only; their captions and the in-text numbers that describe them were used, the graphics themselves were not rendered. Appendices A to D are on OSF and not in the file. No annotation files exist (annot_sha12s empty, n_annots 0), so paul_markup is empty and 0 items were dropped. Key findings: 8 of max 12. Metadata corrections: authors now full names (Soto is Christopher J. Soto per p.5); tag measurement-invariance overstates the paper, which only states that multi-group CFA alignment was run centrally on Field Trial data and reports no invariance results. Internal inconsistency: p.2 says 23 languages, abstract and p.15 say 24. Relevance: no lobbying, networks, path-finding, allocation, elections, persuasion/turnout, legislators or political text measurement content; it is relevant only as Big Five psychometric/translation methodology. Editorial conflicts disclosed on p.20: Rammstedt is Editor-in-Chief; Bluemke and Lechner are Associate Editors.
research_question: How were the BFI-2-S and BFI-2-XS translated and culturally adapted for the PIAAC 2023 social-emotional skills module, so that the 39 resulting language versions are maximally comparable across countries, and can these versions be shared for wider research use?
theory: Big Five trait framework with a hierarchical domain-facet structure (BFI-2). The paper invokes cross-cultural comparability as the rationale for standardized parallel adaptation. It tests no theory.
data: No individual respondent data (Ethics Statement, p.20). Documentary data: 39 BFI-2-XS/BFI-2-S language versions across 29 countries and 24 languages (Table 1, pp.4-11); 15 XS items per version drawn from 30 S items; 1 source instrument. Field Trial data (nearly 30,000 respondents total, roughly 450 to 1,800 per country, pp.3 and 17) were analysed centrally by the PIAAC Consortium but are confidential and not reported. Period: PIAAC Cycle 2 fieldwork 2022/2023, paper received 2024, published January 2025.
method: Descriptive documentation of a modified TRAPD2 procedure (Harkness 2003) with double translation and reconciliation, translation notes, national-centre and domain-expert review, independent linguistic verification, and empirical pretesting. Pre-existing translations (Table 2) were reviewed and adapted. Change requests were coded into a customized MQM error typology (accuracy, accuracy flagged in Field Trial, linguistic convention, style, survey terminology, gender, other). Field Trial psychometrics (descriptives, reliability, EFA, CFA, multi-group CFA alignment) were used to flag national deviations. Results are counts and percentages only; no inferential tests.
identification: None. Descriptive documentation without a causal or comparative inferential design.
scope: Population: adults assessed in the PIAAC 2023 Survey of Adult Skills in the 29 countries that fielded the social-emotional skills module (31 countries participated; Korea, Japan and the United States did not field it in the Main Study). Instrument-level scope: BFI-2-XS in all 39 versions, with BFI-2-S versions for the countries that fielded the longer form. Era: second PIAAC cycle, 2022 to 2023.

key_findings.finding: The paper documents 39 language versions of the BFI-2-XS (and BFI-2-S where fielded) for 29 countries in 24 languages, developed for the PIAAC 2023 Big Five module.
key_findings.location: Abstract p.2; Results and Table 1 pp.4 and 6-11

key_findings.finding: The source instrument is the English BFI-2-XS of 15 short-phrase items, three per Big Five domain, rewritten as full sentences. Responses use a five-point scale with labels strongly disagree to strongly agree, with neutral labeled neither agree nor disagree.

Of 31 participating PIAAC countries, Korea, Japan and the United States did not field the Big Five module in the Main Study. Korea fielded only the BFI-2-S in the Field Trial. Of 28 Main Study countries taking the Big Five, 12 fielded the full 30-item BFI-2-S.
key_findings.location: Countries and Language Regions p.4; Aims p.3
key_findings.numbers: 31 countries; 3 opted out; 12 of 28 took full BFI-2-S

key_findings.finding: For 15 of the 24 languages, pre-existing BFI-2 translations were adapted. For nine languages (12 versions) there were no pre-existing BFI-2-S adaptations, so new translations were produced by double translation and reconciliation.
key_findings.location: Development of the Initial Language Versions pp.15 and 13
key_findings.numbers: 15 of 24 languages pre-existing; 9 languages (12 versions) new

key_findings.finding: Before the Field Trial, change requests on item formulations were coded by MQM category. Gendering accounted for 49 percent (n=37), linguistic conventions 24 percent (n=18) and accuracy 21 percent (n=16). On average 10 percent of BFI-2-S items changed per version, ranging from 0 to 80 percent.
key_findings.location: Review of the Initial Versions pp.16-17; Figure 2
key_findings.numbers: 10% mean item change (0-80% range); 49% gender, 24% linguistic, 21% accuracy

key_findings.finding: Three change requests were judged preferential and not implemented. Requests were approved only when they addressed major issues such as mistranslations that caused Field Trial errors.
key_findings.location: Review of the Initial Versions p.16; Final National Versions p.14

key_findings.finding: After the Field Trial, 13 of the 39 versions requested changes. On average 6 percent of XS items changed per version (range 0 to 53 percent). 46 percent (n=15) of the requested and implemented changes concerned items flagged in the Field Trial; 27 percent (n=9) were other accuracy issues.
key_findings.location: Review of the Tested Versions pp.18 and 17
key_findings.numbers: 13 of 39 versions changed; 6% mean XS item change (0-53%); 46% flagged, 27% other accuracy

key_findings.finding: The authors describe the procedure as fully standardized and run in parallel, and argue this makes the versions more likely to be comparable than independent national translations. They do not report any psychometric evidence supporting that claim, because Field Trial data are confidential.

limitations: Field Trial data are confidential under OECD guidelines, so no empirical psychometric results for the language versions are reported (pp.5 and 19).
The authors state that the versions have not yet been fully validated. The exact psychometric properties of each adaptation, and their comparison with the English source, remain to be studied (p.19).
For languages with both a pre-existing and an adapted version, the paper does not compare them, so it cannot say which is best for research use (p.19).
Table 1 change counts can refer to items not fielded in the Field Trial, and some countries fielded only domains C and O in the Field Trial (Table 1 notes a and c, p.11).
Country-level item-by-item adaptation details, translation notes and the comment spreadsheet sit in OSF appendices, not in the article (pp.3 and 15).
The authors describe the process as time and resource intensive and do not quantify its cost (p.19).
measures: Agreement rating on a five-point scale for 15 BFI-2-XS items (or 30 for BFI-2-S).
Customized MQM error categories for change requests: accuracy, accuracy flagged in Field Trial, linguistic convention, style, survey terminology, gender, other.
Percent of items changed per version before the Field Trial and in the final Main Study version.
references_of_note: Soto and John 2017b, J Res Pers 68:69-81, BFI-2-S and BFI-2-XS source (doi 10.1016/j.jrp.2017.02.004).
Rammstedt, Lechner and Danner 2024, OECD Education Working Paper 311, pilot evidence that BFI-2, BFI-2-S and BFI-2-XS explain comparable variance in PIAAC-relevant outcomes (doi 10.1787/19939019).
Roth, Singh and Lechner 2024, PIAAC Cycle 2 technical report chapter 11, cited as in manuscript preparation (psychometric results source).
Lyberg et al. 2021, AAPOR/WAPOR task force report on quality in comparative surveys.
Roemer et al. 2024, OSF supplementary materials (doi not given in text, osf.io/u4f36) with appendices A to D.

short_quotes.quote: The intention was to take account of the sensitivity of the Big Five items to even slight meaning shifts
The translation and adaptation procedure was fully standardized and conducted in parallel with the aim of achieving fully comparable BFI-2-XS versions
Although all BFI-2-S and BFI-2-XS versions presented here were developed thoroughly, they have not yet been fully validated.
